current_focus.summary: Before implementing checkout or the official payment plugin, align template-store to Commerce 530348c (#14): use Commerce-owned store Inventory configuration and configureCatalogItemInventory with browser input limited to catalogItemId, retain the existing memory layer only as disposable provider/storage proof infrastructure, preserve the neutral Blocks/Commerce/Inventory storefront and shipping deferral, and verify the unchanged desktop/mobile 8-to-5-to-8 stock flow.

decisions.choice: Use a hybrid reference-core model. Commerce owns checkout/order orchestration plus separate payment and shipping provider contracts under one shared descriptor, compatibility, capability, and health envelope. Deterministic non-production providers support local and CI proof. Every production payment processor or shipping-service connection is an installable provider plugin rather than vendor code embedded in Commerce core.

decisions.question: How should concrete payment processors and shipping services connect to DinkusKit Commerce?
decisions.rationale: This keeps a freshly scaffolded template demonstrable without credentials, preserves fail-closed provider behavior, and isolates vendor APIs, credentials, webhooks, and release churn from Commerce core.

decisions.choice: DinkusKit maintains exactly one official payment-provider plugin and one official shipping-provider plugin as separate installable packages conforming to Commerce contracts. Commerce core still ships no production vendor implementation. Deterministic non-production providers remain available for local and CI proof, and additional production integrations may be supplied by the community or store owners.

decisions.question: How many production provider plugins should DinkusKit itself maintain as the supported starter path?
decisions.rationale: One official plugin in each category gives scaffolded stores a supported end-to-end production path while bounding DinkusKit maintenance and keeping vendor-specific APIs, credentials, webhooks, and release cadence outside Commerce core.

decisions.choice: No shipping provider category or vendor is selected in this cycle. Preserve multi-carrier platform, direct-carrier, and manual-fulfillment paths as unresolved candidates until prior integration lessons and current provider behavior are researched.
decisions.deferred_reason: Deferred until Bobby resumes shipping research starting with the existing Katana integration with ShipTheory and Pitney Bowes.

decisions.question: What provider category and concrete service should the one official DinkusKit shipping plugin target?
decisions.rationale: The owner wants additional thought and evidence before establishing the supported shipping boundary; choosing now would turn incomplete recollection into product policy.

decisions.choice: Treat Commerce #14 alignment as a payment-foundation prerequisite. Repin template-store from Commerce 9fd24c6 (#12) to 530348c (#14), replace its direct startManagedSkuRegistration bootstrap with createStoreInventoryConfiguration plus configureCatalogItemInventory, and keep the disposable memory layer only as the local provider and storage adapter. Reprove the existing desktop/mobile 8-to-5-to-8 availability flow before adding checkout or payment behavior.

decisions.question: What consumer baseline must template-store prove before the official payment-provider contract is implemented?
decisions.rationale: PR #3 proves the lower-level registration contract, but it predates the official Configure Inventory action and still lets the consumer assemble site, pool, location, claim, and registration flow itself. Repairing that drift first prevents the payment proof from being built on a storefront integration pattern Commerce has already superseded.

last_pause.next_safe_action: After Bobby authorizes a local commit, commit this bounded template-store alignment, rerun the full verifier against the exact SHA, perform standards and source-intent review, adjudicate findings, then resume the server-owned checkout snapshot and Stripe payment-attempt grill.
last_pause.reason: Commerce #14 consumer alignment is implemented and fully verified locally; exact-source review requires a separately authorized local commit.

alternatives: Implement Commerce price and sellability first, then return to the payment contract with a real authoritative total.
Extend template-store proof through the authenticated Configure Inventory route before starting checkout work.
recommendation.reason: The consumer now follows Commerce #14, but current Commerce still has no price, cart, checkout, order, receipt, or payment implementation. The plugin boundary must begin from server-owned Commerce state and must not accept browser-authored totals.
recommendation.recommended: Define the minimum server-owned checkout snapshot and payment-attempt lifecycle that Commerce will pass to the official Stripe plugin, including authoritative amount, currency, order identity, idempotency, redirect/next-action output, and webhook reconciliation states.
